Activation.description: When a rule runs without being named by its code or name (ADR-018).

oneOf.description:
In the default selection, and matched by a prefix or `ALL`, while the rule is exact;
whatever its certainty with `lint.heuristic`.
Only by its exact code or name.

Selected as an exact `Default` rule is, whatever its certainty: it reports only what a
declared contract asks for, so declaring the contract is what selects it.

Analyzed.description: The files the report was computed from.

errors.description: The files that could not be read or parsed, as `heki check` reports them.

functions.description: The functions in them, module bodies included.

paths.description: The paths given on the command line.

CauseRow.description: The reports that leave one premise or condition open for one cause.

cause.description: The cause, unique within its premise or condition.

closer.description:
What closes the cause: `annotation` (an annotation the user writes, which must be
true), `code` (a change of the code's shape), `heki-catalog` (a fact only heki's
shipped catalog can hold), or `none` (nothing the user can apply to every case).

examples.description: The first 50 reports, in report order.

name.description: The premise's name in the premise table (docs/precision.md), or the condition's.

only_open.description: The reports it is the only open premise or condition of.

reports.description: The reports that leave it open.

rules.description:
The reports by the exact rule whose claim they report and the code they are reported
under.

CauseRule.description: The reports of one rule's claim under one code that leave a cause open.

reported_as.description: The code they are reported under: the rule's own, or its heuristic side's.

rule.description: The exact rule whose claim the reports state.

Closer.description: What closes an open cause, for every case the cause stands for.

oneOf.description: An annotation the user writes; heki trusts it under R2, so it must be true.
A change of the code's shape.
A fact only heki's shipped catalog can hold (no `[[tool.heki.ecosystem]]` key sets it).

Nothing the user can apply to every case: heki cannot establish the premise today, the
code states the opposite, or the cause stands for cases with different closers that the
facts do not tell apart yet.

Combination.description: Causes that reports leave open together.

Consequence.description: What happens in the code a rule reports, which sets its default severity.

oneOf.description:
A bug that can be critical: a wrong result, an exception, a lost update, a deadlock, or a
broken contract.

A bug that is rarely harmful: a promise the code makes is broken, such as a read-only
annotation, where the callers seldom notice.
Slower code that computes the right result.

LeftOut.description:
The Python files below the project root that the paths given leave out: heki takes the
files it analyzed as the whole project.

files.description: The files found, in the order of a walk of the root sorted by name.

python_files.description: How many were found (when `truncated`, a lower bound).

truncated.description:
Whether the count stopped before the end (after 50 files, or after the first 10,000
entries below the root) or could not read an entry.

OpenKind.description:
What a report leaves open: a premise of its claim, which may then be false, or a condition
of the exact tier that is no premise, under which the claim holds.

OpenPremises.description: The heuristic reports of exact claims, by what keeps them heuristic.

by_cause.description:
One row per premise or condition left open and cause, the row that is the only open one
of the most reports first, then the row of the most reports.

by_rule.description: Those reports by the code they are reported under, the most first.

combinations.description:
The sets of more than one cause that reports leave open together, the commonest first:
at most 50.

not_recorded.description: The reports that record no cause, by code: they are counted under no row of `by_cause`.

reports.description:
The heuristic reports of exact claims, as `heki check` prints them with every rule
selected: the heuristic reports of exact rules, and the reports of the heuristic rules
that report an exact rule's claim with a premise open (`EFF111`, `EFF113`).

truncated.description: Whether `combinations` holds fewer sets than there are.

PublishedMeasurement.description:
A measurement as published: the classes of the sampled reports, and the shares derived
from them.

benign.description: Reports that are right, of code that is deliberate or harmless at realistic sizes.

confirmed.description: Reports whose problem is real and observable from the code.

date.description: The date of the build the round measured.

false_claims.description: Reports that are wrong about the code.

plausible.description: Reports that are right, of code that does harm at realistic sizes.

real_harm_percent.description: The share of real harm (confirmed and plausible), in percent.

right_percent.description: The share right about the code (confirmed, plausible, and benign), in percent.

round.description: The round of the measurement protocol.

ReportAt.description: One report, with where it leaves the cause open.

at.description: Where the premise or condition is open: the call of a chain's hop, or a loop.

detail.description: What the cause's statement leaves out: the function, value, or class it is about.

ReportsNow.description:
What the current configuration shows, as `heki check` prints it: reports that share a root
cause are folded into one.

baseline.description: With a baseline: the reports it allows, and the regressions `heki check` prints.

heuristic_rules_off.description: The heuristic rules that are off only because `lint.heuristic` is false.

shown.description: The reports `heki check` prints without a baseline.

withheld_heuristic.description: The heuristic reports of exact rules that `lint.heuristic = false` leaves out.

RuleAdvice.description: One rule the current selection does not run in full.

baseline.description: With a baseline: the added reports it allows, and the regressions.

enabled_now.description:
Whether the current selection runs the rule: then only its heuristic reports, which it
withholds, are counted.

in_block.description: Whether the block enables the rule.

measurement.description: The latest published measurement of how often the rule's reports are right.

reason.description: Why the rule is in the block or not.

reports.description:
The reports naming the rule in `extend-select` would add to what `heki check` prints
(`null` for a rule that is not counted).

oneOf.description: Every rule selected, on the configuration as it is.

description: The JSON object `heki recommend --output-format json` prints.

config.description: The keys `config_toml` adds or changes, as the configuration's keys and values.

config_file.description: The configuration file the run read, or `null` when the project has none.

config_toml.description: The keys to add or change, as TOML for `config_file` (empty when nothing is added).

content.description: The report as the text output prints it.

heki.description: The version of heki that wrote the report.

notes.description: What the reader should know to weigh the advice.

open_premises.description: What keeps the heuristic reports of exact claims heuristic.

root.description: The project root, as the output writes paths (`.` for the working directory).

rules.description:
Every rule the configuration does not run in full: the rules it leaves off, and the exact
rules whose heuristic reports it withholds. The block's rules come first.

runs.description: The analyses the report was computed from, in the order they ran.

table_prefix.description:
The table the configuration's keys are under in that file: `tool.heki` in a
`pyproject.toml`, empty for a file that holds them at its top level (`heki.toml`).

version.description:
The version of the object's fields: it changes when a field is removed or changes
meaning; fields are only added within a version.

title: heki recommend
